programmes.d: A lynch mob wants to hang a young man convicted of killing a family of homesteaders; Bill rides in with a stay of execution from the governor just as the mob is about to break into the jail; the desperate prisoner escapes.

Bill stops to visit his friend, a well-respected sheriff, only to find that the whole town has turned against him, and he's been jailed for killing an unarmed kid; Bill seeks to discover the real truth.
Bill comes to the defense of an unassuming man who is being bullied and tries to encourage him to stand up for himself; soon after, the man asks Bill to teach him how to use a gun.
Bill takes the job of escorting a convicted killer to his hanging, knowing that the man's sons and gang members are planning to free him.
After Neal Wheaton guns down a civilian, Clay makes the tough decision to fire him; Clay orders Neal to leave town.
During an Indian attack, a miner is killed; it's up to Hollister to calm down an angry mob and reason with greedy miners.
Newspaperman Byron Claremont specializes in profiles of gunmen; one of his stories is responsible for an old-time marshal's death; and his next subject is Lucas.
Lucas and Mark lie to protect a dead man's family.
Lucas becomes involved in the family troubles of the hotel clerk.
Fallen ill, a couple seeks shelter with Lucas.
Bat rescues a woman from three assailants and learns that she and her father escaped from the clutches of a gang affiliated with Jesse James, along with proof condemning the outlaws.
The U.S. Army recruits Bat after several enraged Indian tribes accuse white men of abducting their women and children; Bat must find the culprits before a war breaks out.
In Virginia City to check on his silver mine, Yancy finds a gravestone with his name on it.
Yancy wins two tickets to Promontory, Utah, to attend the linking of the transcontinental railroad.
An Easterner and his daughter hire Bill to guide them searching for a wild stallion to breed; however, an old enemy plans to follow them and rob the horse breeder to get revenge on Bill.
Bill goes after the three men who had forced him to accompany them on a bank robbery then framed him for it after.
Josh rushes to Bannach on a dynamite-filled stagecoach hoping to stop the hanging of an innocent man.
Josh hears that the bank robber that he's been trailing has been murdered.
Left to fend for herself and her two children on a remote homestead in the middle of nowhere, a lonely widow strikes up a friendship with a grizzled, restless cowboy.
Daniel Plainview (Daniel Day-Lewis) becomes a self-made oil tycoon, but he deviates into moral bankruptcy as his material fortune grows.
A preacher's son comes to regret the grudge he holds against his father.
Physical and psychological scars torment a man.
A desert denizen meets a woman who changes his life.
A stranger causes unusual events in Heaven, Ariz.
A gambler is suddenly plagued with self-doubt.
A religious leader paradoxically proposes a hanging to preserve the community's pacifist values.
A man is taunted into taking a job escorting a gambler to stand trial.
An imprisoned gunfighter is offered freedom for fighting outlaws.
A gambler's thugs beat up a crusading newspaperman.
A dog leads Cisco and Pancho to his murdered master's gold mine where they become trapped by the victim's killers.
Jake's (Robert Urich) involvement with the Suggs gang reaches a tragic climax; Gus reunites with an old flame (Anjelica Huston).
Gus (Robert Duvall) is injured during an Indian attack; Call (Tommy Lee Jones) has a final run-in with Blue Duck.
A killing and a father's desire for revenge ruins a love affair.
